text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- Switzerland has been invited to the International Nazi Gold Conference that is scheduled to take place in London from December 2 to 4.

- ABB reported slight increases in operating results and net profit for the first six months of 1997 despite a drop in sales. - Gross Immobilien AG in Brugg is filing for bankruptcy. The real estate company has been unable to sell some 80 million Swiss francs worth of property in Canton Aargau.
- Another man, 31-year-old Swiss Silvio Giovanoli, has been arrested in connection with the Nestle drug-dealing case in Guatemala.
- Marco Sassoli, a jurist formerly employed by the International Committee of the Red Cross, has been named Secretary General of the Holocaust Funds.
- Swiss Re says the recent flood damage in Poland, Czech Republic and Germany will cost it some 150 million Swiss francs.
- Daimler Benz is recalling 176,000 Mercedes automobiles due to faulty construction of their electronic systems. Some 3,200 of these vehicles were sold in Switzerland.
- Banque Cantonale Vaudoise posted a six-month gross profit of 68.7 percent to 25.1 million Swiss francs.
